sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The druid's fog was a power some druids possessed. They wrapped themselves in mist and passed by enemies unseen. This mist was also called the féth fiada. The passing druid might become a veil of mist, much like a shape-shifter who becomes an animal. People said the Tuatha Dé Danann received this fog as a consolation prize after they lost Ireland to the Milesians. St. Patrick was also believed to hide himself with this gift. In the poem St. Patrick's Breastplate, he and a companion passed by dangerous druids. The druids saw only a fawn and a deer.
